settings.name: Grok AI Training
settings.description: Three default-on checkboxes control how X feeds your data to xAI. The first allows your public posts, interactions, inputs to Grok, and results to be used for training and fine-tuning. The second allows X to personalize your Grok experience. The third allows Grok to remember your conversation history. All three were enabled by default in 2024 with no user notification.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Opting out stops future data from being used for training. Data already used to train existing model versions cannot be removed. The opt-out is forward-looking only. Making your account private also prevents your posts from being used for Grok training.

settings.name: Data Sharing with Business Partners
settings.description: X shares behavioral data with unnamed business partners for ad targeting and measurement. The policy language is deliberately broad and covers sharing arrangements not individually disclosed to users.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Does not enumerate who the business partners are. Broad policy language may cover data-sharing arrangements not visible to users even after toggling this off.

settings.name: Personalized Ads
settings.description: X uses your on-platform behavior to select ads. Tweets you engage with, accounts you follow, searches, link clicks. Enabled by default.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Turning this off does not stop X from collecting your behavioral data or building your interest profile. You see less relevant ads. The collection continues.

settings.name: Inferred Location for Personalization
webPath: Personalize based on your inferred location
settings.description: X infers location from IP address, device settings, and activity patterns. Used for ad targeting and content personalization without requiring explicit location permission.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Does not prevent IP-based inference. X derives location signals from network data regardless of this setting. The toggle controls use, not collection.

settings.name: Cross-Device Personalization
settings.description: X tracks which devices you use and personalizes content and ads based on cross-device behavior patterns.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Does not stop X from identifying linked devices. It stops using that linkage for personalization, not from detecting it.

settings.name: Track Where You See X Content
webPath: Allow additional information sharing with business partners
settings.description: X monitors when you encounter embedded tweets, X widgets, or X login buttons on external websites. This happens without any interaction on your part.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Does not prevent X from receiving signals when its code is embedded on third-party sites. The toggle controls what X does with those signals, not whether they are received.

settings.name: Discoverability by Email and Phone
settings.description: Two separate toggles let people who have your email address or phone number find your X account. Enabled by default. Also controls whether X can sync your address book to suggest connections.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Disabling these toggles stops new lookups. If someone already found your account through these methods, that connection is not reversed. Previously uploaded contacts are not automatically deleted.

settings.name: Connected Apps
settings.description: Third-party apps authorized via your X account. Each has ongoing access to account data unless revoked.
settings.whatItDoesnt: Revoking permissions stops future access. It does not delete data the app already collected before revocation.
